'''Mitchell Robinson III''' (born April 1, 1998) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Boston Celtics]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA).<ref>{{cite web |title= St. Bernard Gives Back and The Mitchell Robinson III Youth Foundation bring support to SWLA |url= https://www.kplctv.com/2020/09/05/st-bernard-gives-back-mitchell-robinson-iii-youth-foundation-bring-support-swla/ |website=KPLC News|access-date=July 31, 2021 |date=September 5, 2020}}</ref> Before beginning his professional career, he gained national coverage for withdrawing from his commitment to attend [[Western Kentucky Hilltoppers basketball|Western Kentucky University]] to instead dedicate the entire 2017–18 season to training on his own, being the first player to make such a decision. Robinson was selected by the [[New York Knicks]] with the 36th overall pick in the [[2018 NBA draft]]. He won the [[NBA Finals]] with the Knicks in [[2026 NBA Finals|2026]].

==High school career==
[[File:20170329 MCDAAG Mitchell Robinson dunk (4).jpg|thumb|Robinson at the [[2017 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2017 McDonald's All-American Game]]]]
Mitchell Robinson attended [[Pine Forest High School]] in [[Pensacola, Florida]], for the first two years of his high school career, briefly transferring to [[Landry-Walker College and Career Preparatory High School]] in [[New Orleans]] as a sophomore, for whom he never played. He did appear for Pine Forest as a freshman and sophomore, but did not make much of an impact, as he was still relatively new to basketball, only starting playing in eighth grade, during a growth spurt that took him from {{height|ft=6|in=2}} to {{height|ft=7|in=0}}.<ref>{{cite web |title=Pace boys basketball sends a big statement with win vs. Pine Forest |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2013/pace-boys-basketball-sends-a-big-statement-with-win-vs-pine-forest |website=USA TODAY High School Sports |access-date=April 11, 2019 |date=December 4, 2013}}</ref> He first appeared in the summer league before his junior year for [[Chalmette High School]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://highschoolsports.nola.com/news/article/9194770999648085294/chalmette-makes-the-most-of-new-big-man-in-rout-over-salmen-in-summer-league/|title=Chalmette makes the most of new big man in rout over Salmen in summer league|work=The Times Picayune|access-date=July 22, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190721071743/http://highschoolsports.nola.com/news/article/9194770999648085294/chalmette-makes-the-most-of-new-big-man-in-rout-over-salmen-in-summer-league/|archive-date=July 21, 2019|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=http://highschoolsports.nola.com/news/article/-2165067335519238862/mitchell-robinson-transfers-to-chalmette/|title=4-star center Mitchell Robinson enrolls at Chalmette for 2015-16 season|work=The Times Picayune|access-date=July 22, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190721073237/http://highschoolsports.nola.com/news/article/-2165067335519238862/mitchell-robinson-transfers-to-chalmette/|archive-date=July 21, 2019|url-status=dead}}</ref>

As a junior, Robinson led the Owls to their first state playoff win in 19 years, and in the second round, helped give the first seed and eventual state champion [[Natchitoches Central High School]] all they could handle before bowing out, their closest playoff game until the state final. He averaged 20.9 points, 13.6 rebounds, 8.1 blocks, and 2 steals per game. He made the all-district, all-Metro, and all-State teams for his efforts. Robinson then joined [[Dallas]]-based Nike Pro Skills on the [[Amateur Athletic Union|AAU]] circuit for the summer, winning individual honors in the [[Nike EYBL]] and leading Pro Skills to the season-ending Peach Jam. His recruiting ranking shot up, and he earned his fifth star. Against the top players in the country, Robinson averaged 15.5 points, 11.6 rebounds, and 4.1 [[Block (basketball)|blocks]] per game, being named to the All-EYBL second team.<ref>{{cite web |title=Toppers sign 5-star center Mitchell Robinson |url=https://espnky.com/toppers-sign-5-star-center-mitchell-robinson/ |website=ESPNKY |access-date=April 11, 2019 |date=November 16, 2016}}</ref>

As a senior at Chalmette, Robinson averaged 25.7 points, 12.6 rebounds, and six blocks per game, while earning Naismith Trophy All-America honorable mention and [[MaxPreps]] All-America honorable mention status as well as ''[[USA Today]]'' All-USA Louisiana first team honors and being named All-District, All-Metro, All-State, and the All-Metro Player of the Year from ''[[the New Orleans Advocate]]'', as well as the ''St. Bernard Post'' Male Athlete of the Year for the parish.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.usab.com/basketball/players/mens/r/robinson-mitchell.aspx|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180622164925/https://www.usab.com/basketball/players/mens/r/robinson-mitchell.aspx|url-status=dead|archive-date=June 22, 2018|title=Mitchell Robinson|access-date=July 6, 2017}}</ref> He led Chalmette to their first district championship in their own regular season tournament in 20 years, first district title in 21 years in the toughest basketball district in the state, and to the state semifinals for the first time in 32 years.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://highschoolsports.nola.com/news/article/4768411747212344621/chalmette-57-east-jefferson-32-owls-gain-first-outright-district-title-in-21-years/|title=Chalmette 57, East Jefferson 32: Owls gain first outright district title in 21 years|access-date=July 22, 2017|archive-date=July 25, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170725152737/http://highschoolsports.nola.com/news/article/4768411747212344621/chalmette-57-east-jefferson-32-owls-gain-first-outright-district-title-in-21-years/|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=http://highschoolsports.nola.com/news/article/-2376738858449756411/mitchell-robinson-glenshawn-amos-send-chalmette-to-top-28-with-83-69-win-against-helen-cox/|title=Chalmette 83, Helen Cox 69: Mitchell Robinson, Glenshaw Amos send Owls to semis|access-date=July 22, 2017|archive-date=July 25, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170725124141/http://highschoolsports.nola.com/news/article/-2376738858449756411/mitchell-robinson-glenshawn-amos-send-chalmette-to-top-28-with-83-69-win-against-helen-cox/|url-status=dead}}</ref> In the Owls' four-game state playoff run, Robinson averaged 34.5 points, 13.5 rebounds, and 7.8 blocks. Robinson became the first Chalmette basketball player to be named a [[McDonald's All-American]], and also played in the [[Jordan Brand Classic]] and the LHSBCA All-Star game.

Playing in the [[2017 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]], Robinson tallied 14 points, three rebounds, and two blocks.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Page |first=Fletcher |date=April 1, 2017 |title=Mitchell Robinson ready to 'make a difference' at Western Kentucky |work=The Courier-Journal |url=https://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/college/recruiting/2017/04/01/mitchell-robinson-ready-make-difference-western-kentucky/99820876 |access-date=May 22, 2023}}</ref> He participated in the 2017 Jordan Brand Classic, scoring 15 points in 17 minutes of play, while pulling down three rebounds.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://jordanbrandclassic.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/04/2017-Jordan-Brand-Classic-National-Boys-Game.pdf|title=Official Basketball Box Score -- Game Totals -- Final Statistics East Team vs West Team|website=jordanbrandclassic.com|access-date=July 6, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170928010232/http://jordanbrandclassic.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/04/2017-Jordan-Brand-Classic-National-Boys-Game.pdf|archive-date=September 28, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Robinson originally committed to play [[college basketball]] at [[Texas A&M Aggies men's basketball|Texas A&M]], but de-committed to follow coach [[Rick Stansbury]] to [[Western Kentucky Hilltoppers basketball|Western Kentucky]]. Stansbury had recruited Robinson as the Aggies' assistant coach.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/recruiting/basketball/story/_/id/16620936 |title=Ex-A&M recruit commits to Western Kentucky|last=Goodman|first=Jeff|work=ESPN.com|date=June 29, 2016|accessdate=May 22, 2023}}</ref> Basketball writer Jason Frakes wrote in February 2017, Robinson "may go down as the biggest recruiting coup in WKU basketball history."<ref>{{Cite news |last=Frakes |first=Jason |date=February 15, 2017 |title=Top recruit Mitchell Robinson gives hope to WKU basketball fans |work=The Courier-Journal |url=https://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/college/basketball/2017/02/15/top-recruit-robinson-gives-hope-wku-fans/97940130 |access-date=May 22, 2023}}</ref>

==College career==
In July 2017, Robinson enrolled at Western Kentucky University for the summer semester, and practiced with the team for about two weeks before a planned team trip to [[Costa Rica]]. Sources then indicated that he had left campus and his room was cleaned out.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2724343-5-star-c-mitchell-robinson-reportedly-leaves-western-kentucky-campus|title=5-Star C Mitchell Robinson Reportedly Leaves Western Kentucky Campus|last=Chiari|first=Mike|work=Bleacher Report|access-date=August 4, 2017}}</ref> He was then suspended indefinitely for violating the team rules.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/western-kentucky-suspends-5-star-freshman-after-he-bolts-from-campus/|title=Western Kentucky suspends 5-star freshman after he bolts from campus|work=CBSSports.com|access-date=August 4, 2017}}</ref> After speaking with head coach Rick Stansbury, he was granted a release to transfer,<ref>{{Cite news |last=Harten |first=David |date=August 1, 2017 |title=Mitchell Robinson granted release to transfer from WKU |work=The Courier-Journal |url=https://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/college/basketball/2017/08/02/mitchell-robinson-granted-full-release-transfer-wku/531710001 |access-date=May 22, 2023}}</ref> and barring an unexpected decision by the NCAA, would have had to sit out the [[2017–18 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2017–18 season]].

With the hope that a waiver would be granted by the NCAA, Robinson took visits to [[Louisiana State University]], the [[University of Kansas]], and the [[University of New Orleans]] in August 2017.<ref>{{cite news |date=August 17, 2017 |title=5-star recruit Mitchell Robinson expected to pick between UNO, Kansas: source |publisher=nola.com |url=https://www.nola.com/archive/5-star-recruit-mitchell-robinson-expected-to-pick-between-uno-kansas-source/article_df68acf4-9de6-592e-ad00-62e5538a62a9.html |access-date=May 22, 2023}}</ref> On August 27, Robinson returned to Western Kentucky a month after leaving campus.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Roberts |first=Ben |date=August 28, 2017 |title='This is where I want to be': Top recruit Mitchell Robinson is back at Western Kentucky |work=kentucky.com |url=https://www.kentucky.com/sports/college/kentucky-sports/uk-basketball-men/article169755867.html |access-date=May 22, 2023}}</ref>

On September 18, Robinson announced he would forgo college and prepare for the [[2018 NBA draft]] on his own accord.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Five-star big man Mitchell Robinson will bypass college, begin training for 2018 NBA Draft|url=http://scout.com/college/basketball/recruiting/Article/Five-star-big-man-Mitchell-Robinson-will-bypass-college-begin-tr-107602754|website=ScoutHoops.com|access-date=September 18, 2017}}</ref> He would be the first recruited draft pick to not play for any college, professional, or high school/[[postgraduate year|postgraduate]] team throughout an entire year before entering an NBA draft, though the NBA would still credit him as coming out of Western Kentucky.<ref>{{cite web |last=Dauster |first=Rob |title=Mitchell Robinson is not a trailblazer; poor decisions forced him into the worst one-and-done option |url=https://collegebasketball.nbcsports.com/2017/09/18/mitchell-robinson-is-not-a-trailblazer-poor-decisions-forced-him-into-the-worst-one-and-done-option/ |website=CollegeBasketballTalk |access-date=April 11, 2019 |date=September 18, 2017}}</ref> Further, because of his brief time in summer classes at Western Kentucky, League rules barred him from participating in the [[NBA G League]] later in the season.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://uproxx.com/dimemag/nba-prospect-mitchell-robinson-banned-from-g-league/|title=Mitchell Robinson Won't Play In The G League Due To An Obscure Rule|date=January 12, 2018|work=UPROXX|access-date=January 26, 2018}}</ref> The ruling also affected a few similar prospects stuck in difficult situations at the time as well, like [[Billy Preston (basketball)|Billy Preston]] and [[De'Anthony Melton]]. The announcement also influenced at least one person to train by himself for a year before entering an NBA draft, as fellow five-star recruit [[Darius Bazley]] originally planned on not going to college at [[Syracuse University]] to try out for the NBA G League before deciding against that as well.

Robinson was one of 69 players who planned to participate in the [[NBA Draft Combine]]. However, on the day of the combine, Robinson withdrew from all events.

==Professional career==
[[File:Brooklyn Nets vs NY Knicks 2018-10-03 td 176a - 1st Quarter.jpg|thumb|Robinson in 2018]]

===New York Knicks (2018–2026)===

==== 2018–21: Early seasons ====
On June 21, 2018, Robinson was selected with the 36th overall pick in the [[2018 NBA draft]] by the [[New York Knicks]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Guillory |first=William |date=June 22, 2018 |title=Former Chalmette star Mitchell Robinson goes to New York Knicks in NBA Draft 2018 |work=nola.com |url=https://www.nola.com/sports/pelicans/former-chalmette-star-mitchell-robinson-goes-to-new-york-knicks-in-nba-draft-2018/article_e3a05660-d014-50b6-8080-c3436d3e1123.html |access-date=May 22, 2023}}</ref> After appearing for the Knicks in the [[2018 NBA Summer League]], where he set summer league records for blocked shots and offensive rebounds,<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://hoopshype.com/2018/07/15/new-york-knicks-mitchell-robinson-summer-league-draft-steals/|title=Knicks' Mitchell Robinson had most blocks per game in summer league history|work=hoopshype.com|access-date=September 25, 2018}}</ref> he signed a multi-year, rookie-scale contract with the Knicks on July 8, 2018.<ref>{{cite web |title=New York Knicks sign second-round draft pick Mitchell Robinson |url=https://www.nba.com/knicks/front-office-news/new-york-knicks-sign-second-round-draft-pick-mitchell-robinson |website=NBA.com |access-date=November 12, 2018 |date=July 8, 2018}}</ref> After struggling with an ankle injury during the preseason, Robinson made his professional debut on October 17, scoring two points in a 127–106 win against the [[2018–19 Atlanta Hawks season|Atlanta Hawks]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Iseman |first=Chris |title=New York Knicks open season with rout of Atlanta Hawks |url=https://www.northjersey.com/story/sports/nba/knicks/2018/10/17/new-york-knicks-open-season-vs-atlanta-hawks/1675437002/ |website=North Jersey |access-date=December 24, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181104051059/https://www.northjersey.com/story/sports/nba/knicks/2018/10/17/new-york-knicks-open-season-vs-atlanta-hawks/1675437002/ |archive-date=November 4, 2018 |date=October 17, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Hawks vs. Knicks - Box Score - October 17, 2018 - ESPN |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore?gameId=401070697 |website=ESPN.com |access-date=December 24, 2019 |date=October 17, 2018}}</ref> Robinson made his first start on October 26, recording seven points and six rebounds in 29 minutes of action in a 128–100 loss to the [[2018–19 Golden State Warriors season|Golden State Warriors]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Kussoy |first=Howie |title=Fizdale makes big changes to Knicks' starting lineup |url=https://nypost.com/2018/10/26/fizdale-makes-big-changes-to-knicks-starting-lineup/ |website=New York Post |access-date=December 24, 2019 |date=October 26, 2018 |quote=Noah Vonleh, Damyean Dotson and rookie Mitchell Robinson made their first starts of the season...}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Warriors vs. Knicks - Box Score - October 26, 2018 - ESPN |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore?gameId=401070749 |website=ESPN.com |access-date=December 24, 2019 |date=October 26, 2018}}</ref> On November 2, Robinson recorded his first [[double-double]] with 13 points and 10 rebounds, alongside three assists and three steals, in a 118–106 win over the [[2018–19 Dallas Mavericks season|Dallas Mavericks]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Berman |first=Marc |title=Rookies Trier and Robinson dominate as Knicks whip Mavericks |url=https://nypost.com/2018/11/02/rookies-trier-and-robinson-dominate-as-knicks-whip-mavericks/ |website=New York Post |access-date=December 24, 2019 |date=November 2, 2018 |quote=Robinson, the Knicks' new starting center, was a high-flying force on both ends, finishing with 13 points, 10 rebounds, three steals, three assists in 34 minutes, recording his first NBA double-double.}}</ref> On November 11, Robinson set the Knicks' rookie record with nine blocks in a 115–89 loss to the [[2018–19 Orlando Magic season|Orlando Magic]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Berman |first=Marc |title=Knicks' rookie rejection machine puts on an absolute show |url=https://nypost.com/2018/11/12/knicks-rejection-machine-isnt-satisfied-with-record/ |website=New York Post |access-date=November 12, 2018 |date=November 11, 2018}}</ref> On March 28, 2019, Robinson recorded season highs of 19 points and 21 rebounds in the Knicks' 117–92 loss to the [[2018–19 Toronto Raptors season|Toronto Raptors]],<ref>{{cite web |title=Raptors rout Knicks again, win 117-92 without Leonard |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071798 |website=ESPN.com |access-date=March 29, 2019 |date=March 28, 2019}}</ref> and became the first Knicks rookie since [[Willis Reed]] in 1965 to record 19 points and 21 rebounds in a game.<ref>{{cite web |last=Berman |first=Marc |title=David Fizdale wasn't in a positive mood after Knicks' blowout loss |url=https://nypost.com/2019/03/28/kevin-knox-dennis-smith-return-but-knicks-still-get-destroyed/ |website=New York Post |access-date=March 29, 2019 |date=March 28, 2019 |quote=Playing at his active best with alley-oop dunks and putbacks, Robinson still became the first Knicks rookie to log a 19-and-21 ledger since Willis Reed in 1965.}}</ref> On April 9, he recorded eight points and 17 rebounds in a 96–86 win over the [[2018–19 Chicago Bulls season|Chicago Bulls]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Knicks top Bulls 96-86, avoid new franchise low for wins |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071886 |website=ESPN.com |access-date=January 29, 2020 |date=April 9, 2019}}</ref> Robinson finished the season second in the NBA in blocks per game, behind only [[Myles Turner]] of the [[Indiana Pacers]], and was named to the All-Rookie Second Team.<ref>{{cite web |title=Mitchell Robinson gives Knicks a rare victory, earns spot on NBA’s All-Rookie 2nd team |url=https://www.nydailynews.com/sports/basketball/knicks/ny-mitchell-robinson-rookie-team-20190521-vix7v3j4s5da7hiwovhq3mil6u-story.html |last=Bondy |first=Stefan |website=nydailynews.com |access-date=May 22, 2023 |date=May 21, 2019}}</ref>

On December 17, 2019, Robinson scored a career-high 22 points and recorded 13 rebounds in a 143–120 win against the [[2019–20 Atlanta Hawks season|Atlanta Hawks]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Barrett scores 27 as Knicks send Hawks to 5th straight loss |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401161045 |website=ESPN.com |access-date=December 24, 2019 |date=December 17, 2019 |quote=Mitchell Robinson had a career-high 22 points along with 13 rebounds...}}</ref> On January 1, 2020, Robinson scored 22 points on perfect 11-of-11 shooting from the field in a 117–93 win against the [[2019–20 Portland Trail Blazers season|Portland Trail Blazers]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Knicks spoil Anthony's return to MSG, win 3rd straight |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401161147 |website=ESPN.com |access-date=January 2, 2020 |date=January 1, 2020 |quote=Mitchell Robinson made all 11 shots and had 22 points, Julius Randle added 22 points and 13 rebounds...}}</ref> On February 26, Robinson recorded a double-double with 12 points and a season-high 16 rebounds in a 108–101 loss to the [[2019–20 Charlotte Hornets season|Charlotte Hornets]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Perley |first=Sam |title=Hornets Respond with Home Win Over Knicks |url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/hornets-respond-home-win-over-knicks |website=NBA.com |access-date=February 27, 2020 |date=February 26, 2020 |quote=...while Mitchell Robinson added 12 points, a season-high 16 rebounds and three blocks off the bench for his fifth double-double of the campaign}}</ref> When the [[2019–20 NBA season|2019–20 regular season]] finished, Robinson broke [[Wilt Chamberlain]]'s league record for highest field goal percentage in a single season.<ref>{{cite web |last=Berman |first=Marc |title=NBA scraps 'Delete 8' bubble that Knicks never supported |url=https://nypost.com/2020/08/15/nba-delete-8-bubble-scrapped-as-knicks-hope-for-otas/ |website=New York Post |access-date=November 23, 2020 |date=August 15, 2020}}</ref>

On February 12, 2021, in the Knicks' game against the [[2020–21 Washington Wizards season|Washington Wizards]], Robinson fractured his right hand during the second quarter and did not return after halftime.<ref>{{cite web |last=Botte |first=Peter |title=Mitchell Robinson fractures right hand in Knicks win |url=https://nypost.com/2021/02/12/mitchell-robinson-injures-hand-in-knicks-win-over-wizards/ |website=New York Post |access-date=February 19, 2021 |date=February 12, 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Selbe |first=Nick |title=Knicks Center Mitchell Robinson Suffers Fractured Hand vs. Wizards, Will Undergo Surgery |url=https://www.si.com/nba/2021/02/13/knicks-center-mitchell-robinson-fractures-hand |website=Sports Illustrated |access-date=February 19, 2021 |date=February 13, 2021}}</ref> In 72 games (including 62 starts) for the team, he averaged 8.5 points, 8.6 rebounds, and 0.5 assists.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Mitchell Robinson 2021-22 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4351852/type/nba/year/2022|access-date=May 31, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref>

==== 2021–26: Winning years and NBA championship ====
On July 12, 2022, Robinson re-signed with the Knicks on a four-year, $60 million contract.<ref>{{cite web |title=Knicks Re-Sign Mitchell Robinson |url=https://www.nba.com/knicks/news/knicks-re-sign-mitchell-robinson |website=NBA.com |access-date=July 13, 2022 |date=July 12, 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=New York Knicks keeping Mitchell Robinson after agreeing to four-year, $60M deal, agents say |url=https://www.espn.com.au/nba/story/_/id/34179061 |website=ESPN.com |access-date=July 13, 2022 |date=July 1, 2022}}</ref> On November 30, he scored 15 points and grabbed 20 rebounds during a 109–103 loss to the [[2022–23 Milwaukee Bucks season|Milwaukee Bucks]].<ref>[https://www.nba.com/game/mil-vs-nyk-0022200316 GIANNIS (37 PTS, 13 REB) HELPS BUCKS HOLD OFF KNICKS]</ref> Robinson made 59 appearances (58 starts) for New York during the [[2022–23 NBA season]], recording averages of 7.4 points, 9.4 rebounds, and 0.9 assists.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Mitchell Robinson 2022-23 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4351852/type/nba/year/2023|access-date=May 31, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref> In the [[2023–24 NBA season|2023–24 season]], Robinson appeared in 31 games (starting 21) for the Knicks, averaging 5.6 points, 8.5 rebounds, and 0.6 assists.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Mitchell Robinson 2023-24 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4351852/type/nba/year/2024|access-date=May 31, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref>

On September 23, 2024, it was announced that Robinson would miss the beginning of the regular season after offseason ankle surgery.<ref>{{cite web |title=Sources: Knicks' Robinson to miss start of season |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/41401141/sources-knicks-mitchell-robinson-miss-start-season |website=ESPN.com |access-date=24 September 2024 |language=en |date=23 September 2024}}</ref> On February 28, 2025, Robinson returned and put up six points and five rebounds in a 114–113 win over the [[2024–25 Memphis Grizzlies season|Memphis Grizzlies]].<ref>{{cite web |date=February 28, 2025 |title=Knicks' Mitchell Robinson makes season debut in win vs. Grizzlies |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/44061301/knicks-mitchell-robinson-makes-season-debut-win-vs-grizzlies |access-date=March 7, 2025 |website=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press}}</ref> In his injury-truncated season, Robinson logged averages of 5.1 points and 5.9 rebounds over 17 games.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Mitchell Robinson 2024-25 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4351852/type/nba/year/2025|access-date=May 31, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref>

On March 13, 2026, Robinson put up a career-high 22 rebounds in a 101–92 win over the [[2025–26 Indiana Pacers season|Indiana Pacers]].<ref>{{cite === Boston Celtics (2026–present) ===
On July 6, 2026, Robinson signed a three-year, $47.4 million contract with the [[Boston Celtics]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Celtics, Mitchell Robinson Complete Three-Year Deal |url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2026/07/celtics-mitchell-robinson-agree-to-three-year-deal.html |access-date=July 6, 2026 |website=Hoops Rumors}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/press-release-20260707-celtics-sign-mitchell-robinson|title=Celtics Sign Mitchell Robinson|work=NBA.com|date=July 7, 2026}}</ref>

==National team career==
Robinson was named to the preliminary roster of the [[United States men's national under-19 basketball team|United States national under-19 team]] in 2017, but did not make the final cut for the 12-man squad for the [[2017 FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup]].<ref>{{Cite news |last= |first= |title=Robinson doesn't make final cut for USA U19 team |url=http://www.bgdailynews.com/sports/wku/robinson-doesn-t-make-final-cut-for-usa-u-team/article_ab72d018-67c3-5b6f-b54b-da35b553ac46.html |access-date=July 6, 2017 |work=Bowling Green Daily News}}</ref>

At the tryout, Robinson measured {{height|ft=7|in=0}} without shoes, {{height|ft=7|in=1}} with shoes, {{convert|223|lb}}, with a {{height|ft=7|in=4}} wingspan and {{height|ft=9|in=3}} standing reach.<ref>{{cite web |title=Mitchell Robinson - NBADraft.net |url=https://www.nbadraft.net/players/mitchell-robinson |access-date=April 11, 2019 |website=nbadraft.net}}</ref>

==Player profile==
Robinson has been called by some analysts "the best shot blocker in his class", with uncommon closing speed and a long reach that led to numerous highlight-reel blocks. He uses that speed also to run the fast break exceptionally well for a big man of his size, being called the "most entertaining player" in the New Orleans area for his ability to convert [[alley-oop]] dunks. Robinson improved his free throw shooting performance over the course of his two years at Chalmette High School, and developed range from behind the [[three-point line]], making as many as five in a game. Prior to Robinson's joining the NBA, draft projections compared his game to [[DeAndre Jordan]] and [[Tyson Chandler]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Phillips |first=Scott |date=August 17, 2016 |title=CBB Recruits with the Best Chance to Play for Team USA in Tokyo 2020 |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2658006-cbb-recruits-with-the-best-chance-to-play-for-team-usa-in-tokyo-2020 |access-date=May 22, 2023 |website=Bleacher Report}}</ref> 

Since entering the NBA in 2018, Robinson’s shot diet has consisted completely of dunks and layups. He has neither made nor attempted any three-point shots during his NBA career.<ref>https://www.statmuse.com/nba/ask/mitchell-robinson-stats-by-year</ref> His primary strength is his offensive rebounding ability, with offensive rebounding rates that rank the highest in NBA history.

Robinson has been noted for his exceptionally poor [[free throw]] shooting. His career free throw percentage is the lowest in NBA history.<ref>{{cite web |first=Steven | last=Simineri | date=December 11, 2025 |title= Knicks' Mitchell Robinson is Making Brutal Free Throw History |url= https://www.si.com/nba/knicks/onsi/news/new-york-knicks-mitchell-robinson-brutal-free-throw-history |access-date=June 14, 2026 |website= Sports Illustrated}}</ref> During the Knicks’ championship-winning 2025-26 season, Robinson shot 40.8% from the line.<ref>https://www.statmuse.com/nba/ask/mitchell-robinson-free-throw-percentage </ref> His playoff free throw percentage—29.3%—was the lowest in NBA playoff history.<ref>https://www.statmuse.com/nba/ask/mitchell-robinson-free-throw-percentage-in-playoffs</ref> Basketball commentators have attributed Robinson’s historically poor free throw ability to his habit of shooting with “zero arc” from the line.<ref>{{cite web |first=Steven | last=Simineri | date=December 11, 2025 |title= Knicks' Mitchell Robinson is Making Brutal Free Throw History |url= https://www.si.com/nba/knicks/onsi/news/new-york-knicks-mitchell-robinson-brutal-free-throw-history |access-date=June 14, 2026 |website= Sports Illustrated}}</ref> Other teams have exploited Robinson's poor free-throw performance by employing a "[[Hack-a-Shaq|Hack-a-Mitch]]" tactic, intentionally fouling Robinson to send him to the free throw line and get possession of the ball.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Phillips |first1=Ryan | last2=Silverman |first2=Blake | date=June 5, 2016 |title= Spurs Use Hack-a-Mitch Strategy in NBA Finals to Limit Knicks Offense|url= https://www.si.com/nba/finals/spurs-hack-a-mitch-strategy-nba-finals-to-limit-knicks-offense |access-date=June 14, 2026 |website= Sports Illustrated}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Robinson lives in [[White Plains, New York]] and has a daughter named Riley, born in 2023. Robinson is a [[truck]] enthusiast and has multiple custom [[pickup trucks]].<ref name="d907">{{cite web | title=Basketball Coverage on Instagram: "Mitchell loves his trucks" | website=Instagram | date=2026-05-09 | url=https://www.instagram.com/p/DYH6B3YDe61/ | access-date=2026-05-10}}</ref><ref name="v780">{{cite web | last=Binoy | first=Allan | title=The wild reason Knicks' Mitch Robinson won't make Joel Embiid poster his phone background | website=Yahoo Sports | date=2026-05-09 | url=https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/wild-reason-knicks-mitch-robinson-071020990.html | access-date=2026-05-10}}</ref> Robinson also enjoys listening to [[country music]].<ref>{{citeweb|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/country-music-helped-knicks-mitchell-085516997.html|title=How country music helped Knicks' Mitchell Robinson shut down Victor Wembanyama when it mattered most|last=Talbot|first=Nick|publisher=[[Yahoo Sports]]|date=June 6, 2026|accessdate=July 7, 2026}}</ref>
